description:
User directed 2026-11-19: "add the elixir parity issues as tickets to the epic we gave to Elixir Parity". Owner: Elixir Parity. Found by Elixir Parity. The port's decoders() @type (otp_json.ex:865) is %{optional(:array_start) => array_start_fun(), ...}; decode_value() uses %{optional(binary()) => decode_value()}. fz's type parser rejects them: 'a map type key must be a literal atom or int'. Done: both parse and declare types on three paths; a self-oracle fixture covers them.

## Scope (widened 2026-11-19, corrected the same day)
A map type key may be any type, as in Elixir (lib/elixir/pages/references/typespecs.md:137):
- %{key_type => value_type} with a non-literal key is a map with required pairs, the same as required(K).
- optional(K) and required(K) are written explicitly.
- Typespec maps are closed: a map containing a key outside the allowed keys does not belong to the type, and %{} is the empty map.
Today %{atom => v} and %{binary() | atom() | integer() | float() => v} fail with 'a map type key must be a literal atom or int'. Needed by fz-9zq.6's R6 probes and by json.erl's encode_map/decode_value.

## Size
This is a lattice change, not a parser fix. MapSig holds only required literal atom/int keys and is always open. Key domains and optional fields are ported from Elixir's descr.ex. Elixir Parity writes a proposal page with the user's decisions before building.

comments.text: Widened 2026-11-19 (Elixir Parity, Coordinator). A bare non-literal key, e.g. %{atom => v} or %{binary() | atom() | integer() | float() => v}, fails with 'a map type key must be a literal atom or int'. Elixir reads it as optional(K). Needed by fz-9zq.6's R6 probes and by json.erl's encode_map/decode_value. optional(K)/required(K) stay in scope.
CORRECTION to the 04:33 comment: a bare non-literal key means required pairs, not optional(K), and typespec maps are closed. The description now carries the corrected scope.

title: A map type key may be any type, as in Elixir
